name: SIGGRAPH
fullName: ACM SIGGRAPH Conference on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques
notes: The submission form and conflicts are due one week before the paper. The Technical Papers page publishes these dates; detailed 2027 submission instructions and the review timeline are still pending.

publication.note: Journal and conference paper tracks are distinct. 2027 publication details are pending; journal route verified from 2026.

paperFit.scope: Graphics algorithms, rendering and visual content
paperFit.emphasis: Visual quality, control and measured performance

guide.contribution: Methods for representing, generating or rendering visual content. Contributions improve visual quality, artistic control or computational performance, using geometry, physical models or learning to produce convincing results across varied inputs.
guide.evidence: Visual comparisons are paired with task-specific measurements: reconstruction or rendering error, control accuracy, runtime and scaling. Experiments vary scenes, inputs and operating conditions; generative work also measures human preference, while display work validates results on physical prototypes.

comparisons.difference: SIGGRAPH and SIGGRAPH Asia publish rendering, geometry and simulation methods. For either venue, show the visual change and measure its cost: image error, geometric accuracy, runtime or memory.

SIGGRAPH includes rendering, displays and static geometry as well as animation. SCA focuses on moving characters and simulated materials: evaluate motion timing, contacts, controllability and physical behavior.

name: SIGGRAPH Asia
fullName: ACM SIGGRAPH Conference on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques in Asia
notes: Journal and conference papers share deadlines. New submissions and author-list changes close at the abstract deadline. The extra upload day only permits files matching previously submitted MD5 checksums. The 2027 event is announced; its paper deadlines are not. Decision release has no exact time.

publication.note: Journal and conference paper tracks are distinct.

guide.contribution: Algorithms and representations for rendering, simulation and shape processing. Connect the mathematical formulation to a working implementation that improves image quality, simulation stability, geometric detail or scalability.
guide.evidence: Compare visual output and numerical quality against relevant methods while accounting for runtime. Evaluations examine dynamic-scene response, simulation compression and stability, mesh discretization and learned deformation quality, with experiments that expose the effects of individual algorithmic choices.

comparisons.difference: SIGGRAPH Asia and SIGGRAPH publish graphics algorithms supported by visual results and numerical comparisons. Rendering quality, simulation stability and geometry processing are relevant to either venue.

SIGGRAPH Asia and Eurographics publish rendering and geometry methods. SIGGRAPH Asia work measures rendering noise, simulation stability and deformation quality; Eurographics work also tests memory use, sparse motion inputs and capture conditions.

name: Eurographics
fullName: Annual Conference of the European Association for Computer Graphics
notes: Full papers track. Submission dates include the published extensions; later deadlines use UTC. The author list locks at abstract submission. The CFP also notes submission-system delays, so projected dates should not rely on extensions recurring. Decision releases have no exact times.

core.note: Older CORE edition; no ICORE2026 entry found.

publication.note: Accepted full papers publish in CGF; other contribution types may use proceedings.

guide.contribution: Graphics methods that improve representation, computation or capture. Address a clear technical constraint, such as memory use, sparse motion controls or limited sensing, and demonstrate the improvement across relevant inputs.
guide.evidence: Measure accuracy and visual quality alongside the resource or input constraints being addressed. Experiments compare memory and runtime, examine difficult geometries and levels of detail, and test reconstruction across motion styles, datasets and real-world capture conditions.

comparisons.difference: Eurographics and SIGGRAPH publish geometry, rendering and motion methods. Eurographics work tests resource limits and sparse input data; SIGGRAPH work also evaluates camera control and physical display prototypes.

Eurographics includes static geometry and rendering algorithms, evaluated through accuracy, memory and runtime. SCA focuses on animation and simulation, where motion sequences, contacts and temporal coherence become central measurements.

name: SCA
fullName: ACM SIGGRAPH / Eurographics Symposium on Computer Animation
notes: Full papers appear in Computer Graphics Forum. The Important Dates table is used for the review schedule; CFP prose has an inconsistent June 16 first-round notification. Only abstract and paper dates specify a time; other milestones remain date-only.

publication.note: Accepted full papers publish in CGF; other contribution types may use proceedings.

paperFit.emphasis: Temporal behavior, controllability and physical plausibility

guide.contribution: Methods for generating, controlling or simulating animated content. Contributions improve motion editing, temporal coherence, contact handling or physical dynamics, with clear control over the resulting animation.
guide.evidence: Show animated sequences that reveal timing, contacts and changes in control. Learned methods use held-out sequences, comparisons and ablations, including collision and reconstruction measurements; other experiments demonstrate style, timing and trajectory edits or detailed dynamics at interactive rates.

comparisons.difference: SCA focuses on how characters and materials move: show motion control, contact handling or simulation behavior over time. SIGGRAPH includes those topics plus rendering, displays and static geometry.
SCA work tests motion representations, collisions and cloth dynamics. MIG also studies how people use animation and interaction systems, measuring task performance, control and user feedback.

name: MIG
fullName: ACM SIGGRAPH Conference on Motion, Interaction and Games
notes: Long and short papers share a deadline, extended from August 7. There is no rebuttal process. Accepted work requires an in-person presenter. Notification release has no exact time.

publication.note: Selected best papers may be referred (subject to validation) to submit substantially extended versions to a special issue. Journal publication requires further review.

guide.contribution: Animation, simulation and interaction methods for authoring tools, games and immersive experiences. Connect motion control, material behavior or interaction design to a working system and the task it supports.
guide.evidence: Evaluate the behavior that the system changes: constraint accuracy and motion examples for authoring, material response and comparisons for simulation, or task performance and participant feedback for interaction. Working application examples connect technical improvements to actual use.

comparisons.difference: MIG and SCA publish motion synthesis and simulation. MIG also evaluates interactive uses, such as authoring controls or haptic assistance; SCA work concentrates on motion coherence, collision handling and physical dynamics.

MIG connects animation and simulation methods to authoring or interactive tasks, measuring control and usability. Eurographics also includes static geometry and rendering systems, measured through accuracy, memory and runtime.

name: CEIG
notes: Full papers track. The live official page extends the paper date to February 15. Short papers, posters and presentations of published work have separate deadlines. Journal-selected papers undergo additional review. No exact cutoff time is published.

core.note: No matching entry found by acronym and full title; this is not an Unranked classification.

publication.note: Selected C&G papers receive an additional major review. Graphical Models requires a 30% extension and further review; selection does not guarantee journal acceptance.

paperFit.scope: Graphics methods and applied visual computing
paperFit.emphasis: Working systems, measured accuracy and efficiency

guide.contribution: Focused graphics methods and applied visual-computing systems. Improve reconstruction, appearance modeling or geometry processing, with a clear technical contribution to an application or computational bottleneck.
guide.evidence: Demonstrate the complete pipeline on representative data and quantify the relevant trade-offs. Evaluations measure reconstruction or alignment error, success rate, runtime, memory and image similarity, with visual results that show whether the method preserves useful geometric or appearance detail.

comparisons.difference: CEIG work evaluates complete reconstruction and appearance pipelines using alignment error, success rate and processing cost. Eurographics also develops reusable rendering, geometry and motion methods, tested across input data and resource constraints.

CEIG work includes static reconstruction, appearance modeling and geometry processing. MIG focuses on animation tools and interactive experiences, where motion behavior, task performance and user control are part of the evaluation.

name: SGP
notes: Final submission round. The first 2026 round closed February 4 (recommended abstract February 2). The recommended early abstract date is not mandatory. SGP 2027 is announced within IGS in Singapore, June 21–25; SGP-specific event dates and submission deadlines are not yet published. The 2026 submission page does not specify cutoff times.

publication.note: Technical papers appear in a Computer Graphics Forum issue following a two-stage review.

guide.contribution: Algorithms, mathematical formulations, representations and datasets for processing geometric shapes. Contributions improve meshing, deformation, registration, distance fields or shape analysis, with a clear advance in geometric properties, numerical behavior or computational efficiency.
guide.evidence: Measure geometric error, robustness and computational cost across shapes and input conditions. Support mathematical guarantees with analysis, and compare numerical behavior with established methods. Dataset contributions need coverage analysis, documented annotations and baseline results on tasks such as shape matching or retrieval.

comparisons.difference: SGP specializes in geometry processing, including shape representations, meshing and geometric algorithms. Eurographics includes these topics within a broader graphics program covering rendering, animation and visual computing. Geometry-focused methods can fit both.

SGP centers on the geometric method: accuracy, robustness, mathematical properties and efficiency. SIGGRAPH also publishes geometry processing, alongside rendering, animation and visual systems. A geometric algorithm with strong analysis and practical results can suit either venue.
